prompt:
Render a single finished 1536x1024 consumer product website screenshot for a fictional compact outdoor camera named FIELD 01. Art-direct it as a credible 2026 Liquid Glass web interpretation: photographic content is the stage, while only navigation and a small purchase control use a translucent material. The result is a real product page with readable functions, not a moodboard, a material swatch poster, or a collection of floating cards. No real brand logos. The wordmark FIELD is simple original sans-serif typography.

A beautifully lit graphite compact camera rests on a broad river stone in a shallow stream. The camera has a believable fixed lens, a knurled dial, a subtle textured grip and convincing proportions. Compose the product at a large scale slightly right of center, with the stream, gray stones and a modest patch of green moss extending continuously across the full page. Natural daylight creates soft directional reflections. The palette comes from real material: stone gray, off-white light, graphite, restrained moss green. No neon cyan, rainbow holographic wash, violet gradient, chrome sci-fi pedestal or glowing particles. This is sophisticated product photography with tactile detail and generous calm zones around the interface.

Across the upper edge place one slender floating navigation bar with a single outer capsule contour and four simple textual regions: FIELD, Camera, Journal, Support. Use dark crisp labels on a mostly opaque light material. There are NO individual outlined capsule rings around each label. The bar has a soft inner edge highlight, a subtle dark lower edge and localized optical bending of the photographic texture directly underneath its boundary. Refraction belongs only to the material edge; the text itself is never distorted, blurred, outlined or embossed. The center of the bar has enough opacity to make every label readable. This is believable adaptive glass, not a rectangle containing a sharp duplicated photograph.

Integrate a compact editorial heading directly on a calm image area in the upper-left/middle-left: 'FIELD 01' with a smaller line 'A pocket camera. A 28 mm view.' Keep the heading at a realistic product-page scale, approximately 44–56px in a 1536px screenshot. Use a refined plain sans-serif, absolutely no dramatic italic or oversized luxury serif. Do not put the heading and camera into separate left/right boxed panels; the photograph remains one continuous environment. A compact two-line specification below reads '28 mm fixed lens' and 'Weather-sealed body'. These are text, not equal-sized feature cards or floating chips.

Near the lower-left place one dark filled primary button labelled 'Explore Field 01'. It has a comfortable click area and simple rounded corners. No duplicated Buy Now buttons, no extra demo CTA, no glowing arrow, no pricing card grid. Along the lower edge, a quiet white product-information band begins, with the readable text 'Small enough for every day.' and a small 'View specifications' text link, giving the sense of a real scrollable page. The page should look thoughtfully designed, with consistent baseline alignment, real spacing and no filler slogan stacks. Keep content panels stable and opaque. At most two glass surfaces are visible and this design should use only the navigation as its main glass surface.

Render fine light refraction and edge reflections clearly enough to identify the material, but never sacrifice content readability. No browser chrome, no desktop frame, no phones, no people, no fake chat widget, no cookie modal, no badge cloud, no stars, no watermark, no unused background blobs. Every visible control has a clear product purpose. Produce one polished full-bleed website screenshot with legible exact short text and a coherent hierarchy.
negativeConstraints: No duplicate playback controls, no nested capsule outlines, no opaque content made glass, no generic giant serif hero, no watermark, no illegible text.
priorFailureAnalysis: Main and independent audit found excessive outlined glass controls and a weak content-control hierarchy; mobile source also duplicates playback controls in a desktop layout.

prompt:
Render one complete 1536x1024 landscape mobile music player screen, designed for a large foldable mobile device in landscape. This is ONE mobile app view, not a desktop dashboard, not three phone mockups, not a browser window, and not several screen variants. No device bezel or exterior frame. The fictional music service is called TIDE. Use a mature, uncluttered Liquid Glass-inspired material system: a stable content image and one floating playback control layer, with no glass over every content panel.

The background is original album art: a quiet photographic view of a rocky coastline in clear morning light, pale natural sky, muted blue-gray water, charcoal rocks and one understated ochre accent in a small beach structure far away. It should feel like an intentionally chosen album cover rather than a generic blue glacier fantasy. The landscape image runs continuously across most of the screen. It has calm darker zones where white text remains readable, without a blurred full-screen overlay. No rainbow aura, holographic ring, glowing tunnel, artificial nebula, music-note particles or isolated 3D icons.

Top-left is a small near-opaque back control and the text 'Now playing'. Top-right has one simple queue icon button; do not add a left sidebar, Home/Search/Radio navigation list, a permanent up-next column or a desktop settings rail. Navigation is extremely sparse. Use consistent thin custom line icons, never emoji. A small TIDE wordmark can appear in the top center without dominating the screen.

In the lower-middle area above the controls, set the track title 'Slow Morning' in a crisp substantial but not oversized sans-serif. Beneath it the artist 'Juniper Coast' and the album 'Low Tide'. Keep these labels on the image's calm area with a subtle local darkening scrim if needed, not a separate glass card. Place one modest save/bookmark icon beside the track information, not a large Saved pill. No duplicate track information elsewhere.

The sole playback surface is a wide low floating translucent toolbar near the bottom, inset evenly from the screen edges. It contains exactly ONE progress track, one elapsed label '1:32', one duration label '4:06', and one set of previous, pause and next controls. The progress knob is around 37 percent of the track. The pause control is the dominant central control; neighboring controls are smaller and clearly spaced for touch. A small volume icon may be present only if it does not form another playback strip. There is no second mini-player at the bottom or side. The overall toolbar is one continuous rounded form with a single exterior contour; no nested capsule outline around each child. Active control fills can be opaque but should not create a row of ringed pills.

Material appearance: a very subtle dark lower edge, bright but restrained upper rim, localized refraction of coastline detail along the toolbar perimeter, and a sufficiently opaque neutral body behind text. The album art's line where water meets rock may visibly bend at a small segment of the material edge, demonstrating refraction. Text, icons and hit targets stay geometrically stable and sharp; glass never distorts the controls themselves. No excessive glossy bubbles, lens flare or oil-slick rainbow. Mobile hierarchy and one coherent playback task matter more than ornament. The rest of the content remains a stable image plane.

Use realistic mobile spacing, clear contrast, one intentional accent and readable text. No marketing hero, fake analytics, features grid, tiny illegible text blocks, browser chrome, window buttons, stock logos, watermarks or multiple screens. The final artifact is a polished, believable landscape mobile player that could be operated comfortably, with a single refined Liquid Glass control surface.
negativeConstraints: No duplicate playback controls, no nested capsule outlines, no opaque content made glass, no generic giant serif hero, no watermark, no illegible text.
